extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP firm managers, corporate IP counsel, and researchers of legal economics
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of survey metrics and categories from the AIPLA Report of the Economic Survey 2023 covering billing practices, median litigation costs by case type and amount at risk, post-grant proceeding costs, dispute-resolution costs, and firm characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Fee Primarily Used in 2022 — Filing US Applications Abroad (Europe/EPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveyed which fee type (fixed fee, hourly, other) was primarily used in 2022 for specific foreign-filing services related to filing US applications abroad (Europe, EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services most likely billed hourly include: patent application amendment/argument where US counsel or the client provides foreign counsel with detailed response instructions — relatively complex mechanical (69.0%), minimal complexity (69.0%), relatively complex biotechnology/chemical (67.7%), relatively complex electrical/computer (65.0%). Services most likely billed on a fixed-fee basis include: paying an annuity or maintenance fee (60.5% fixed), entering national stage in foreign Receiving Office from US-origin PCT application (46.2% fixed), filing US-origin utility patent application in foreign office received ready for filing with formal papers (43.2% fixed). Charted as percent fixed/hourly/other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Fee Primarily Used in 2022 — Other US Patents and Copyrights
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveyed primary fee types (fixed fee, hourly, other) for services under 'Other US Patents and Copyrights' in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services most likely billed hourly include responding to Office action in design patent application (67.7%) and US plant patent application preparation/filing (57.5%). Services most likely billed on fixed fee include copyright registration application (preparation/filing) (53.1%), US design patent application (preparation/filing) (52.1%), preparing and filing international design patent application under the Hague Agreement (46.3%). Chart provides breakdown by fixed/hourly/other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Fee Primarily Used in 2022 — Transactional Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveyed primary fee types for transactional IP work in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactional services overwhelmingly billed hourly: due diligence (92.9% hourly) and preparing licenses, including negotiations (92.2% hourly). Charted fixed/hourly/other percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Patent Infringement (All Varieties) by Amount At Risk and Phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Median (and quartile/mean) litigation costs for patent infringement matters across different amounts at risk (Less than $1M; $1–$10M; $10–$25M; >$25M) and by litigation phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs reported for distinct phases: Initial case management; Inclusive of discovery, motions, and claim construction; Inclusive of pretrial/trial/post-trial and appeal (when applicable); Cost if dispute was resolved through mediation. Tables and charts show 1st quartile, median, mean, and 3rd quartile values across survey years (2014–2022). The report also notes mapping of new varieties to historical categories for temporal comparisons and cautions about approximate comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Patent Infringement Pursuant to the Hatch‑Waxman Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs for ANDA/Hatch‑Waxman patent litigation segmented by amount at risk and by litigation phase (same phase categories as general patent infringement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports quartiles/median/mean for phases: initial case management; inclusive of discovery/motions/claim construction; inclusive of pre/post-trial and appeal; mediation cost. Values shown across survey years and risk bands, with numeric examples in thousands of dollars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Patent Infringement (Defending Claims by Non‑Practicing Entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs when defending claims of patent infringement asserted by non‑practicing entities (NPEs), by amount at risk and phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same phase breakdowns and quartile statistics as other patent categories; tables present the medians/means/ quartiles per risk band and across years (2014–2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Patent Infringement, Section 337 (ITC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs for Section 337 patent infringement actions at the International Trade Commission, by amount at risk and by phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase breakdowns (initial case management; inclusive discovery/motions/claim construction; inclusive pre/post-trial & appeal; cost if resolved through mediation) with quartile and mean statistics shown across years and risk categories. Separate PGR/IPR-style rows are shown for life sciences, electrical/computer, and mechanical where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Trademark Infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs for trademark infringement actions, broken down by amount at risk and by litigation phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides quartile/median/mean values for each phase (initial case management; inclusive discovery/motions/claim construction; inclusive pre/post-trial & appeal; cost if resolved through mediation) and across risk bands and survey years. Also includes respondent perceptions of correlation between amount at risk and attorney hours for trademark cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Trademark Opposition/Cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated costs for trademark opposition/cancellation proceedings reported through filing petition, through end of discovery, and inclusive all costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides medians/means/quartiles (small-dollar ranges) for the three listed stages (new in 2021 revisions) and shows typical values for those stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Copyright Infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs for copyright infringement cases, by amount at risk and by litigation phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-based quartile/median/mean reporting similar to other categories, across risk bands. Also includes respondent-reported correlation statistics between amount at risk and attorney hours for copyright actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Median Litigation Costs — Trade Secret Misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Median litigation costs for trade-secret misappropriation suits, broken down by amount at risk and by litigation phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase-based statistics (initial case management; inclusive discovery/motions/claim construction; inclusive pre/post-trial & appeal; mediation) with quartile/median/mean values across risk bands and years. Includes respondent perception metrics on correlation and cost comparison for trade-secret suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated Total Cost of Filing or Defending PGR/IPR — By Technology and Stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated total costs (1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile) of filing or defending post‑grant proceedings (PGR/IPR) by technology area (Life Sciences; Electrical/Computer; Mechanical) and by stage (through filing petition; through end of motion practice; through PTAB hearing; through appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts provide numeric values (in thousands) for each stage and technology. Also reports respondents' view that filing a petition often costs about the same as defending (59.7% say 'about the same'), with the remainder reporting filing averages 85.2% of defending cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation Between Amount At Risk and Attorney Hours Required
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey question asking whether respondents observe a strong correlation between the amount at risk in an action and overall attorney hours required to litigate the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported 'Yes' percentages by dispute type: patent infringement (70.3% yes), trademark infringement (69.7% yes), copyright infringement (71.4% yes), trade secret misappropriation (81.8% yes). Guidance: summary statements note strong correlation for the majority of respondents in each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Cost Comparison — Asserting vs Defending an Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveyed respondents' comparison of total cost of asserting an infringement action to the total cost of defending such an action; reported as 'about the same' proportion and as an average percent (asserting as percent of defending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided in the report: patent infringement — 63.4% say 'about the same' and others report asserting averages 96.4% of defending; trademark — ~79.0% 'about the same' and average asserting as 119.7% of defending; copyright — 81.8% 'about the same' and others reporting asserting averages 60.5% of defending; trade secret — 81.3% 'about the same' and others reporting asserting averages 90.6% of defending. The report presents these comparisons by dispute type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimated Total Cost of a Patent Infringement Suit — Phase Quartiles and Risk Bands
rubrics_metrics.description: Charts and tables providing 1st quartile, median, mean, and 3rd quartile estimates for patent infringement suits at different amounts at risk and for different litigation phases (summarized across 'All Varieties').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric examples shown (e.g., less than $1M at risk: initial case management median $28k, inclusive discovery median $300k, inclusive pre/post-trial median $600k; higher risk bands show larger medians). Presented graphically by risk band and phase to illustrate cost escalation with amount at risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Cost of Resolving Dispute Through Arbitration vs Litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent-reported comparisons of total cost resolving disputes through arbitration versus litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 38.8% reported costs are 'about the same'; others reported the average cost of arbitration as 77.7% of the cost of litigation. The report also notes initiation reasons for mediation/arbitration (based on contract 47.5%; mandated by court 29.2%; voluntarily by parties 23.3%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and Basis for Initiation of Mediation/Arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: How mediation/arbitration was initiated in 2022 (based on contract terms; mandated by court; voluntarily by parties) and comparative trends versus prior surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2022 percentages: based on terms of contract 47.5% (higher than prior years), mandated by court 29.2% (similar to prior years), voluntarily by parties 23.3%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Firms Engaged in IP Practice — Firm Size, Offices, and Work Patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey data on private law firm characteristics: number of attorneys, number of offices, planned office closures, percentage of employees working remotely, percent of practice devoted to IP, and proportion of solo practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the report: responding firms (n=157) had distributions across attorney counts (e.g., increases in firms with 3–5 attorneys), 66.9% reported one major office location, average number of office locations was 3.7 in 2022, 94.2% do not plan to close major offices in 2023/2024, 24.0% reported reducing/planning to reduce office space, average remote work in 2022 was 56.8% of employees (reported 53.8% for 2023), 79.7% of firms reported IP accounted for three-quarters or more of their practice, and 20.5% reported being a solo practitioner. The report notes typical respondent role (managing partner/shareholder 66.0%).
